statements.venue: Press release announcing the AI Regulator Act proposal
statements.quote: The Federal Digital Commission would keep pace with innovation, act before serious harm occurs, and have the authority to hold companies accountable when they break the rules.
statements.context: Bennet and Sen. Welch announced a proposal for a federal commission with power to review frontier AI models and delay releases that could pose catastrophic risk.
statements.reason: His own quoted words speak only of "serious harm" in general terms; the catastrophic-risk wording is in the release's headline and description of the proposal, not in his quote.

slowdown.note: His AI Regulator Act proposal would require pre-clearance of frontier AI models and let a commission delay public release of models with potential catastrophic risk for up to six months or until safeguards exist, but he also said "we should innovate" and "I want us to lead the Chinese". This is a conditional brake on release, not a call to slow capability progress in general; a reviewer may prefer "none".

pause.note: The proposed power to pause is over public release of specific risky models, not a halt to building more capable frontier AI; no statement for or against a development pause was found.

intl.note: He is not among the signers of the 23 September 2026 letter urging AI talks with China. He said no one but President Trump thinks the US and China see eye to eye on AI, which is not a statement against an agreement.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI.

record: Announced with Sen. Welch the proposed AI Regulator Act: a five-member Federal Digital Commission with pre-certification of frontier AI models, power to pause public release of models with potential catastrophic risk for up to six months, catastrophic-risk incident reporting, and penalties up to 15 percent of prior-year global revenue.
Issued a statement opposing President Trump's executive order blocking state AI laws (about protecting children and consumers, not catastrophic risk).
Joined a statement with Sens. Shaheen, Coons and others opposing the export of Nvidia H200 AI chips to China (page title only; not opened).
Joined Sen. Schatz and colleagues in a letter pressing Meta on children's use of AI chatbots (page title only; not opened).
grade_reason: In two September 2026 interviews, reproduced on his own Senate site, he said AI models could threaten the extinction of humanity and that warnings that humanity could be destroyed by AI must be heeded.
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. Both A quotes come from interview excerpts on Bennet's own Senate press release of 25 Sep 2026, which I read in full; I did not view the CNN or Bloomberg video. The quotes use the release's punctuation (curly apostrophes) and its transcription, including "find these guys" (probably "fine"). The CNN interview is dated 2026-09-24 because the 25 Sep release says "last night". The Bloomberg interview date is not given on the release (only "this week"); 2026-09-25 is the release date, so the interview was on or shortly before it. Not on the verified signer list of the 23 Sep 2026 China letter. No source found showing he co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (reported sponsors are Sanders and Casar); the congress.gov cosponsor page could not be opened (403), so co-sponsorship is unconfirmed either way. The Axios Denver article of 17 Sep 2026 could not be opened (403); a search summary attributed to him the words "Congress will never be able to move fast enough", left out as unverified and not about catastrophic risk. Colorado Politics (1 Nov 2026) mentions his vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act, with no quote from him. The 16 Dec 2025 statement on the state-law executive order and the China chip-export statements are level D and were left out of statements. The slowdown value of "mixed" is a judgment call explained in its note.
